newsitem.title: USA: Sacramento, Calif., seeks approval for arena debt.
newsitem.headline: Sacramento, Calif., seeks approval for arena debt.

text.p: The city of Sacramento has asked a judge to clear the way for its proposed sale of up to $80 million of notes to refinance a basketball arena, attorneys said on Tuesday.

The city asked a Sacramento Superior Court judge to "validate" the deal. The validation process should clear away the legal challenges facing the deal and enable the city to issue the notes in the coming months, city attorneys said.
"If the court validates it ... that would end any question," said Norman Hile, one of the city's attorneys. "We're trying to get things done as quickly as possible."
The Sacramento City Council approved the note plan in February in a bid to keep the National Basketball Association Kings playing in the city.
With the proceeds of the note sale, the city would refinance $51.5 million of Arco Arena debt, where the Kings play. The remaining note proceeds would be used to refinance other franchise debts.
The notes were expected to be sold earlier this month. The deal was put on hold, however, after at least two lawsuits were filed against the city's proposal.
If the Superior Court judge validates the deal, attorneys for the city would seek to dismiss the lawsuits. A hearing date has yet to be set on validation.
